title: Spreading a finite algebra from the generic fibre
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$, and let
$T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be
projective.
Every finite coherent
$\mathcal O_{T_K}$-algebra extends to a finite
$\mathcal O_{T_{A[a^{-1}]}}$-algebra for some $0\ne a\in A$.
A finite product decomposition of the generic algebra can be extended
at the same time.

proof.text: Put $S=A\setminus\{0\}$, directed by divisibility, and $A_a=A[1/a]$. The cited localization-colimit lemma gives $K=\varinjlim_{a\in S}A_a$. Each $A_a$ is Noetherian: an ideal $J\subset A_a$ is generated by the images of any finite generators of its contraction to $A$, since $x/a^n\in J$ implies $x/1\in J$. The affine-limit lemma therefore identifies $\operatorname{Spec}K$ as the limit of $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$. These affine schemes are qcqs by the affine-scheme lemma. The scheme-over-limit lemma gives $T_K=\varprojlim_a T_a$, where $T_a=T\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, with affine transition maps.

The projective-proper lemma makes $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper, hence separated and of finite type by the definition of proper. Thus it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated by the separated-quasi-separated lemma, and locally of finite presentation by the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma. It is consequently of finite presentation. Base-change permanence gives these three properties for every $T_a\to\operatorname{Spec}A_a$. The qcqs-over-affine lemma shows each $T_a$ is qcqs. These are precisely the geometric hypotheses of the module-descent and eventual-zero-map lemmas used below.

source.place: Tags 01W8, 01WC (locally projective implies proper), 01TX; schemes Tags 01KK, 01KU

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the given generic algebra and $M$ its underlying module. Coherent-local-finite-presentation gives local finite free presentations of $M$; the finite-presentation/quasi-coherence lemma makes $M$ quasi-coherent. Apply module-map descent, clause (1), with initial stage $a=1$, to obtain a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $M_a$ on $T_a$ and an isomorphism $(M_a)_K\simeq M$.

For any two finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $F,G$ on a stage, their tensor product is quasi-coherent with affine sections $F(U)\otimes G(U)$ by the cited tensor lemma. It is finitely presented: if $F(U)=R^p/\langle r_1,\ldots,r_s\rangle$ and $G(U)=R^q/\langle t_1,\ldots,t_v\rangle$, its presentation has generators $e_i\otimes e_j$ and the finite relations $r_k\otimes e_j$ and $e_i\otimes t_l$. The affine finite-presentation criterion applies. This also proves finite presentation of the triple tensor. Pulling back any stage module preserves finite presentation by the cited pullback lemma; tensor pullback is identified with tensor of pullbacks by the tensor comparison, and $f^*\mathcal O=\mathcal O$ by $R'\otimes_R R\simeq R'$ locally.

source.place: Modules Tags 01CD, 01AO, 01BO; properties Tag 01PC; finite presentation matrices written explicitly

proof.text: Via $(M_a)_K\simeq M$ and the tensor comparison, regard the multiplication and unit of $\mathcal C$ as maps $(M_a\otimes M_a)_K\to(M_a)_K$ and $(\mathcal O_{T_a})_K\to(M_a)_K$. Clause (2) of module-map descent lifts both to some common later stage: $\mu_b:M_b\otimes M_b\to M_b$ and $u_b:\mathcal O_{T_b}\to M_b$. A common stage exists by directedness (take a product of the finitely many indices), and previous lifts are pulled back. If a finite product decomposition of $\mathcal C$ is specified, also lift the finitely many maps $e_i:\mathcal O_{T_K}\to M$ corresponding to its coordinate idempotents. All these sources and targets have finite presentation by step 4.

source.place: Tag 01ZR (2), applied to multiplication, unit and the finite family of idempotent sections

proof.text: On $T_b$ form the differences of the two associativity maps $M_b^{\otimes3}\to M_b$, of $\mu_b$ and $\mu_b\circ\tau$ on $M_b^{\otimes2}$, and of each of the left and right unit maps and $\mathrm{id}_{M_b}$. The usual associators and unitors are used in these formulas. Their generic pullbacks vanish: on pure tensors the comparison sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to the same triple of pullbacks, so the resulting equations are exactly $(xy)z=x(yz)$, $xy=yx$, $1x=x=x1$ in $\mathcal C$. Apply eventual-zero-map descent separately to these four defects, then choose one common later stage. Their sources are finite type (indeed finitely presented by step 4), their targets are finitely presented, and $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-compact by step 2. If idempotents were lifted, do the same for the finitely many maps $\mathcal O\to M_b$ representing $e_i^2-e_i$, $e_ie_j$ for $i\ne j$, and $\sum_i e_i-u_b$. Their generic pullbacks are zero. Thus all algebra identities and all product identities hold on one $T_c$.

source.place: Tag 01ZR (3); eventual vanishing for the explicit finite list of defects

proof.text: The maps $\mu_c,u_c$ now make $M_c$ a sheaf of commutative unital $\mathcal O_{T_c}$-algebras: bilinearity gives distributivity and central scalar multiplication, and the four imposed identities give associativity, commutativity and the two unit laws. The fixed generic module isomorphism respects multiplication and unit by their lifting construction, hence is an algebra isomorphism. The affine finite-presentation criterion implies $M_c$ is locally finitely generated as a module; this is the meaning of a finite quasi-coherent algebra. Thus it is the required finite algebra extending $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 01ZR; algebra structure from its multiplication and unit identities

proof.text: For a specified decomposition with $r>0$ factors, set $\mathcal C_i=\operatorname{Im}(e_i\cdot-:M_c\to M_c)$. The cited image lemma makes these quasi-coherent and computes their affine sections as $e_iM_c(U)$. Such a module is generated by $e_i$ times any finite set of generators of $M_c(U)$, so the affine finite-type criterion makes each factor finite. Each image is an algebra with unit $e_i$, with structure map $t\mapsto te_i$. The homomorphism $M_c\to\prod_i\mathcal C_i$, $x\mapsto(e_ix)_i$, has inverse $(x_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i x_i$: the composites are identities by $\sum e_i=1$ and $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$. These formulas are valid on every open and commute with restriction, so give an algebra-sheaf product decomposition. After generic pullback the same formulas identify these factors with the prescribed ones: multiplication by $e_i$ is a split projection, and any functor preserves its splitting equations. A zero factor, $e_i=0$, causes no problem.

source.place: Tag 01ZR (2)-(3) finite diagrams; schemes Tag 01IB for quasi-coherent images; elementary orthogonal-idempotent calculation

proof.text: If the specified product is empty, its algebra is the zero algebra, which extends as the zero algebra on $T$ (choose $c=1$). Otherwise the common index $c$ above is a product of finitely many nonzero elements of $A$, so $c\ne0$ since $A$ is a domain. Renaming $c$ as $a$ gives exactly the asserted principal localization. Empty $T$ and the zero generic algebra are allowed throughout: rank-zero presentations and the displayed identities remain valid.

source.place: Tag 01ZR construction; zero objects and the product of finitely many nonzero denominators

proof.text: The preceding steps prove the stronger finite-product assertion spread_finite_algebra_product. For spread_finite_algebra, take the singleton index type PUnit, all factors equal to C and its sole projection the identity. The fan with vertex C and this projection is limiting: a cone factors through its only leg, and uniqueness follows from that same leg. Apply the product assertion and retain its localization, base-change maps, finite quasi-coherent algebra and scalar-extension pushout; discard the factor data. This uses the same stronger assertion in this node, with no new obligation.

source.place: Non-product assertion as the one-factor case of the finite-product assertion

proof_origin.place: Original nine-step plan retained for spread_finite_algebra_product; spread_finite_algebra is its singleton-factor corollary (U5).
